title: Continuous Audit and Assurance
answer: Ledger anomaly detection, substantive testing, inventory observation, going concern analysis and controls testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Ledger Anomaly Detection
children.blurb: Ledger anomaly detection is the practice of scanning general ledger and subledger entries for items that depart from expected patterns, including duplicate postings, unusual account combinations, round amounts, odd posting times, and late top-side adjustments.

children.name: Substantive Testing at Full Coverage
children.blurb: Substantive testing at full coverage means applying audit procedures to every item in a defined population rather than to a sample.

children.name: Inventory Observation and Valuation
children.blurb: Inventory observation and valuation covers the evidence that inventory exists, is owned or controlled, is complete, is in saleable condition, and is carried at the right amount in the financial statements.

children.name: Going Concern Analysis
children.blurb: Going concern analysis in continuous audit and assurance is the ongoing evaluation of whether an entity can meet its obligations and continue operating for the foreseeable future.

children.name: Internal Control Testing
children.blurb: Internal control testing covers the design and operating effectiveness of controls that support reliable financial reporting, compliance and operations.

sections.body: Continuous audit and assurance is the use of AI to monitor financial records, transactions, and controls on an ongoing basis rather than only at period end. In practice, AI systems scan ledgers for unusual patterns, flag transactions that deviate from expected behavior, and help auditors decide where to look. They can run substantive testing across entire populations instead of samples, which changes the economics of audit work. Inventory observation uses computer vision and sensor data to count and value goods, sometimes remotely. Going concern analysis uses models to track liquidity, covenant, and market signals over time. Internal control testing uses automation to check whether approvals, reconciliations, and segregation of duties are working as designed.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, such as rule based anomaly detection and automated reconciliation checks, which are widely used in finance functions. Full coverage substantive testing is technically possible for structured data, but it depends on clean data pipelines and clear audit trails. Inventory observation with drones, cameras, and AI counting is promising but still limited by physical conditions, tagging, and valuation assumptions. Going concern analysis remains difficult because it mixes quantitative signals with judgment about future financing and management plans. Internal control testing can be automated for routine controls, yet many controls are manual, judgment based, or embedded in spreadsheets. The honest limits include false positives, model opacity, data quality, and the need for auditor judgment that cannot be fully delegated, and the site tracks 222 compliance and regulation pages, which reflects how much of this work is shaped by rules and oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a chain from detection to conclusion, and a reader would go to each for a specific part of the assurance workflow. Ledger Anomaly Detection is the entry point for finding unusual transactions and patterns in the general ledger. Substantive Testing at Full Coverage explains how AI moves testing from samples to populations and what that means for evidence. Inventory Observation and Valuation covers the physical and valuation side, where AI meets counting, condition, and cost. Going Concern Analysis deals with the forward looking question of whether an entity can continue, using signals and scenarios. Internal Control Testing addresses the design and operating effectiveness of controls that underpin reliable reporting, and together these pages show how continuous audit is assembled rather than bought as one system.
